label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Dear Appa, Amma, Kiran, Divya and all,

Before I get into the practicalities, I want to say plainly how happy this news has made me. I cannot wait to have Amma and Appa here. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, which includes “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”, and Rohan is fully expecting a vegetable patch transformation.

Kiran, you are right that I should have brought you in before the visa paperwork began. I started it because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, but I should have called you then rather than leaving you to find out once things were already moving. That was my mistake, and I’m sorry.

For the history of it, rather than as an excuse, the idea first came from Appa. We were on the phone in August while Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on video, and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” I loved that thought and got carried away with making it practical. I should have slowed down and involved you properly.

Your three concerns all deserve proper answers.

On Appa’s heart: yes, we need a clear plan, not just an assumption that everything will be fine. The application is for the UK long-term visitor visa, which allows a maximum of six months per visit; the proposed dates are the first week of April to the end of September 2027. I have a six-month travel-insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, at about £640 each. The agent says it covers Appa’s stent, and I will share the full policy wording so we can all look at exactly what that means rather than relying on a verbal assurance.

Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before they fly and to do a video consultation in July. He is also happy to share Appa’s notes with me. Leicester Royal is 15 minutes from our house, and I know a lot of the cardiology team there. None of that guarantees that nothing will happen, but we will have Dr. Prakash’s advice, the relevant records, appropriate insurance and a hospital close by. We would not be relying on visitors receiving free NHS treatment. If anything in the March review means the plan should change, then we change it.

The annexe at the back is now finished as well. It is all on the ground floor, with no steps, and has its own shower with a grab rail, so Amma and Appa will have their own comfortable space.

Your point about Amma is fair too. Six months is a long time, and I don’t want her to feel that by agreeing to come she has committed to staying that long regardless of how she feels. The return ticket will be flexible. She can go home at any point — after six weeks, earlier, or whenever she wants. Amma, please know that this is your choice, not an obligation to us.

And yes, Kiran, Pune and Ganesh Chaturthi should have been part of the discussion from the beginning. One possibility is for Amma and Appa to fly from Leicester to Pune for the festival in September and finish their trip there. Another would be for you, Divya and the children to come here in August. I would genuinely love that, and I would like to cover the flights for your whole family. We can talk through both possibilities and, most importantly, hear what Amma and Appa would like.

Could we all have a family video call this Sunday at 4pm UK time / 9.30pm India time? It would be better to discuss the health arrangements, the length of the stay and Pune together than to try to settle everything over email.

I’m glad you raised these things, Kiran. I should have involved you sooner, and I will from here. I’m still incredibly excited about having Amma and Appa here — I just want us to do it thoughtfully, together, and in a way that feels good to all of us, especially them.

Love,
Meera
